task.description:
Work through the provided tools to repair the project according to the task.
Existing source files may be edited; tests are read-only. outline provides Python
structure; read_file provides exact numbered source. verify runs the fixed tests
and returns full results in every condition. finish ends your attempt; acceptance
is evaluated separately on a fresh snapshot using the original tests.
Automatic conditions run those same tests synchronously after each successful
source-changing edit. Check receipts and failures describe the check, not task
acceptance. An unchanged edit or rejected edit does not run a hook. An execution
error, timeout or stale check must be investigated. Full evidence handles can be
retrieved through read_output/search_output. Choose economical steps; finish once
you have evidence your implementation satisfies the task.

Condition: Automatic checks return a success receipt or failure diagnostics after source-changing edits.
Task: Implement the missing KVEntry and KVStore methods according to their docstrings. JSON snapshots are objects mapping string keys to string values; import merges them into the store without TTL. Preserve expiration and deletion contracts.
Files: engine.py, models.py, test_contract.py

function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.
function.name: glob_files

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.
function.name: read_file

function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.
function.name: outline

function.description: Search case-sensitive literal text by default, or Python regex with regex=true. Returns one line per matching line as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers; context_lines adds surrounding lines. file_glob only selects which files are searched.
function.name: search_text

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

query.description: Required. Literal text, or a Python pattern when regex=true.

function.description: Replace literal text in a file, treating LF and CRLF line endings as equivalent. Preserve existing bytes outside the replacement and use local line endings for new_text. Other whitespace must match exactly. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.
function.name: replace_text

function.description: Apply a single-file unified diff to an existing file. Exact line positions and context must match; all hunks are validated before writing. LF/CRLF differences are tolerated and local endings preserved. Supply path and patch (optional ---/+++ headers followed by @@ hunks). Use write_file to create files.
function.name: apply_patch

function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.
function.name: write_file

function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.
function.name: read_output

function.description: Search an earlier output for literal text or optional Python regex, with surrounding context.
function.name: search_output

function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.
function.name: finish

function.description: Run the fixed project tests. Full results are returned; this tool is available in all conditions.
function.name: verify
